Subject: Strange stalls after private handoff (traces + pcap attached)

Jordan —

We finished the private handoff to your VPC connector at ~02:30 PT last night. Most traffic looks fine, but our app team started seeing intermittent TCP stalls to the internal database tier in our on-prem datacenter — connections hang for 15-30 seconds before succeeding.

Attached are a short traceroute and a tcpdump showing SYN retries and then a sudden forward progress. We also have a handful of successful flows that look identical until one hop where packets stop for ~20 seconds then resume.

What we checked locally:
- firewall rules: no denies for peer CIDRs
- DB server iptables conntrack not overloaded
- host MTU is 1500

Can your team take a look? We suspect an asymmetric path or a translation issue on the private glue.

Samir

Attachments:
- harbormed-trace-20270529.txt (traceroute + route table)
- tcpdump-syn-retrans.pcap (10MB stub)

Thanks — I pulled the pcap. Quick notes:
- SYNs go out from HarborMed, get SYN-ACK, then our edge ACKs but there's a ~18–22s gap before further payload.
- No immediate RSTs observed from our edge.
- Conntrack at the edge shows a short-lived SYN_RECV -> ESTABLISHED transition with a gap; counts don't indicate global conntrack exhaustion.
- SNAT pool usage peaked but stayed within pool limits. No SNAT port exhaustion for the time window in the monitoring graphs.

Two hypotheses:
1) Asymmetric return path: some intermediate hop is black-holing data for a burst then forwarding, maybe due to microflow steering being unstable on a transit device.
2) MTU fragmentation + MSS clamp mismatch: if middlebox clamps and then intermittently drops fragments we'd see stalls until path MTU discovery completes and retransmits smaller segments.

Quick checks I recommend HarborMed run (low friction):
- curl -v --http1.1 from an app host to DB with tcpdump in parallel to capture the moment of stall
- run ping -s 1472 to test PMTU across path

I'm going to pull BGP state for the handoff window and check next-hop flaps.

-Karthik

I pulled the BGP + route logs for the private connector at the handoff time:
- There was a short-lived route update from the transit partner that adjusted the ECMP next-hop set for HarborMed prefixes. Update lasted ~22s and then reverted. No BGP session resets.
- We also logged a transient route-suppression event on the forwarding plane where the dataplane temporarily preferred a control-plane-sourced route with a different nexthop set — it looks like programmatic route suppression (the dataplane deprioritized an older path while it reconciled adjacency).

This aligns well with the observed ~20s holds. If a flow is pinned to a nexthop that suddenly becomes de-prioritized on the dataplane without immediate pin rehash, packets could be queued/dropped until the pin moves.

Vanessa — can you pull firewall logs and show whether we saw state drops corresponding to the timestamps? If not, it looks like phantom dataplane pinning.

-Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: Strange stalls after private handoff (traces + pcap attached)

I pulled edge firewall / SG logs for the time window. Findings:
- No explicit DENY or RESET entries for HarborMed flows.
- We saw short-lived gaps in the state table for a handful of flows — those entries had state=PENDING for ~18–24s before moving to ESTABLISHED.
- No evidence of security group rate-limiting or L7 drops.

Given Marissa/Karthik notes, this looks like a dataplane route pinning quirk during ECMP set churn. Two actionable mitigations:
1) Temporarily pin HarborMed prefixes to a single preferred nexthop to avoid ECMP rehash during their cutover window.
2) Enable faster rehash (lower pin timeout) for the connector in question — has some risk but will reduce stalls if pinning is the root cause.

I propose we coordinate with HarborMed to run a short test: we will pin their prefix to the current best nexthop for 30 minutes and ask their app team to run a burst test to validate. If stalls disappear, we escalate a dataplane fix to product.

-Vanessa

Samir — quick status and recommended next steps after internal triage:

What we saw:
- Short ECMP next-hop set churn from our transit partner at the handoff time.
- Dataplane route suppression caused pinned flows to experience ~18–24s pending state before rehash.
- No SNAT exhaustion, no SG denies, MTU checks OK on both ends.

Immediate remediation (we executed with HarborMed consent):
1) We pinned HarborMed prefix to the preferred nexthop for a 60-minute window starting 2027-05-30T12:15:00Z.
2) HarborMed ran a burst test (10s high RPS) during that window. Result: no stalls observed, flows remained steady.
3) We opened NET-2248 to track a dataplane fix (lower pin-timeout + improved rehash) and engaged the transit partner for a root-cause blameless postmortem.

Follow-ups for PM:
- Engineering will draft a short KB for runbooks during private handoffs recommending temporary prefix pinning for customers performing large cutovers.
- Product to consider exposing a one-click temporary pin option in the Console for Dedicated/Private connectors.

Samir — apologies for the impact during your cutover. Thanks for fast logs and patience. Let us know if you want the playbook and a runbook we can run together for your next maintenance window.

-Jordan
